name: JetLevel
roleBasis: Its pricing page says: "JetLevel is a broker. We price real trips across many operators every day."
summary: Broker that publishes median all-in trip prices from its own quote data, with sample sizes.
differentiator: The only one of the 22 providers we read that publishes total-trip medians with sample sizes (3,220 quotes, 500 operators, 210 aircraft models) and explains why its hourly figures are higher than advertised base rates: they include positioning, crew, fees and tax. The dataset is its own and the page does not date it.
priceNote: Hourly figures are the total quoted trip price divided by flight time, so they include positioning, crew expenses, landing and handling fees and the 7.5% federal excise tax. It also publishes one-way and round-trip medians by distance and aircraft class.
operatorDisclosure: Not stated on the pages we read.
bestFor: Buyers who want a realistic total to expect rather than a base rate, and want to see how many quotes sit behind each number.
skipIf: You want base hourly rates. Its figures are not base rates.
